newsitem.title: KENYA: Airlift of Rwandan refugees starts in earnest.
newsitem.headline: Airlift of Rwandan refugees starts in earnest.

text.p: A total of 186 Rwandan refugee children flew out of the Zairean city of Kisangani on Wednesday for Rwanda at the start of a U.N. airlift, the U.N. refugee agency said.
"An Ilyushin has taken off with 186 unaccompanied minors bound for Kigali. A second plane is due to go any minute with 50 refugees bound for Gisenyi in Rwanda," said UNHCR spokesman Peter Kessler.
"This is the start of the airlift which we hope will break the logjam and get these refugees home," said Kessler, adding UNHCR hoped to have two more Ilyushin flights to Rwanda later on Wednesday.
Each of the Russian-made planes can take 220 passengers.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila gave U.N. agencies 60 days from Thursday to return all Rwandan refugees in Zaire to Rwanda.

U.N. officials said it was impossible to repatriate all 100,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees scattered south of Kisangani and another 250,000 Rwandan refugees who are unaccounted for in Zaire within the next 60 days even with full rebel cooperation.
